answer: One concrete mechanism: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because delta only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, ember is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any meadow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
